dropped.why: Virtual reality isn’t in the first release. AR is its own work (WP21, WP22).
Shapes are Props now, so they use width, height and depth like every other model.
Set by the stage for the device, or a second way to do the same thing. Filming uses the vertical viewing angle and shot types.
The ground and the sky stay where they are.
Aids for Alice’s own scene editor, not story blocks.
Java’s string editing, left over on Alice’s text model. `getValue` and `setValue` stay.
Dragging objects while a film plays. It would share the screen with the scene view’s drag handles (7.1) and the Rehearse controls, and it’s pointer-only (decision 0051).
It fires on every frame while an object moves, which is hard for a young programmer to reason about. Proximity, collision, timers and the `follow` shot cover most uses (decision 0051).
Waiting for a measurement. Each pair of objects is tested from the camera on every frame. S3 measures that on the reference devices, then the owner decides (decision 0051).
A handler gets the key itself, so it can compare it. `numberKeyPress` covers digits.
Only the keys listed under `Key` are kept: function keys, keypads and input-method keys are left out, because many school keyboards and iPads lack them.
“As often as possible” can’t work with a time-slice budget, so a timer always has a number of seconds.
